data.title: Prince Harry, others ordered to pay Daily Mail £9.5 million
data.description: LONDON - A British court ordered Prince Harry and six others on Friday to pay an initial £9.5 million ($13 million) after they lost their privacy case against the publisher of the Daily Mail.

data.title: Sword-wielding man injures several at Swedish school
data.description: STOCKHOLM - A man armed with a sword injured several people at a Swedish high school on Friday and one person was later detained, local ​authorities said.

data.title: Pope to visit San Marino, address Italian political event
data.description: VATICAN CITY - Pope Leo XIV will travel to the tiny republic of San Marino on Saturday before attending a cultural and political event organised by an influential Catholic group at an Italian seaside resort.

data.title: Meghan faces difficult return to the UK
data.description: LONDON - Prince Harry’s wife, Meghan, faces a tough challenge in reassimilating to life in the UK where she remains deeply unpopular, as well as managing uneasy ties with the royal family.

data.title: Maresca needs time to succeed after ‘big changes’ at Man City
data.description: LONDON - Enzo Maresca insists he can replicate Manchester City’s success under Pep Guardiola if he is given time to handle the “big changes” at the club.

data.title: Romania holding suspect linked to weapons cache in Germany
data.description: BERLIN - Romania is holding a suspected “low-level agent” accused of preparing attacks, following the discovery of handguns and ammunition in a forest near Berlin, Germany’s interior minister said Friday.

data.title: Expelled student apologises for school shooting threat in Hat Yai
data.description: SONGKHLA - A 14-year-old former student has apologised after posting social media messages threatening to carry out a shooting at a school in Hat Yai district of this southern province, prompting a police investigation.

data.title: Iran wants to end war while in a ‘position of strength’
data.description: TEHRAN - Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Friday it was time to end the months-long Middle East war with the United States because Tehran appeared to be in a stronger position than Washington.

data.title: 44 Thais repatriated from Cambodia
data.description: Thai security authorities received 44 Thai nationals returning from Cambodia at the Ban Khlong Luek border checkpoint in Aranyaprathet district of Sa Kaeo province on Friday, with five wanted on arrest warrants.

data.title: ICC head warns against ‘demise of international rule of law’
data.description: TOKYO - International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane of Japan warned on Friday against “the demise of international rule of law” after the United States targeted her with sanctions.

data.title: Ebola ‘growing exponentially’ in DR Congo
data.description: GENEVA - The Ebola outbreak raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo is growing “exponentially”, with more than 2,500 deaths recorded and half of those in the last 20 days, the senior UN coordinator on the disease said on Friday.

data.title: Chiang Mai city buses returning to the roads
data.description: City buses will resume services in Chiang Mai this month, after soaring fuel prices forced the operator to pull the fleet off the streets for the first time in eight years.

data.title: Flooding persists in six provinces
data.description: Flooding continues to affect six provinces in Thailand, with more than 73,000 people impacted, while some areas have begun recovery efforts as water levels recede, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM).

data.title: 600 rai of illegal durian plantations to be cleared in Trat
data.description: TRAT - Authorities are preparing to clear more than 600 rai of illegal durian plantations around the Huai Raeng reservoir in Muang district of this eastern province as part of a crackdown on encroachment by investors.

data.title: Premier League returns with Arsenal eyeing title dynasty
data.description: LONDON - Champions Arsenal kick off the Premier League season on Friday (2am Saturday Thailand time) reinforced by astute signings as boss Mikel Arteta welcomes the pressure of being “hunted” by their title rivals.

data.title: Indian court orders new steps to protect elephants
data.description: NEW DELHI - India’s top court has ordered tough new steps to protect wild elephant herds as habitat loss and human-elephant conflict intensify, a move welcomed by campaigners on Friday.

data.title: Guru's Weekly Buzz: Aug 21-27
data.description: Guru By Bangkok Post's weekly pick of the most exciting products, activities, food and travel to indulge in.

data.title: Gateway to a world of flavour
data.description: <p>Auckland is best-known for its harbour views and multicultural vibe, though with the Michelin Guide's foray into New Zealand, it gives travellers just one more reason to visit, especially with five Michelin-starred restaurants.</p>

data.title: Restaurant consoles customer who left ominous order note
data.description: A restaurant owner in Thailand has shared how a seemingly innocuous note left on a food delivery order prompted him and his partner to contact a customer, who was going through an emotional crisis and had intended the meal to be her last.

data.title: Two new plant species discovered in Tak national park
data.description: Two plant species previously unknown to science have been discovered in Khun Phawo National Park in Tak province, the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation (DNP) said.

data.title: Scientists uncover how cats identify each other by urine scent
data.description: Domestic cats identify each other by sniffing their urine, as their urinary composition profiles are individually distinctive, according to a study published in a scientific journal.

data.title: Australia charges man with trying to pass Ukraine military intel to Russia
data.description: SYDNEY - Australian police charged a man with foreign interference on Friday for allegedly seeking to pass intelligence about Ukrainian military activities to Russia.

data.title: 600 rai of illegal durian plantations to be cleared in Trat
data.description: TRAT - Authorities are preparing to clear more than 600 rai of illegal durian plantations around the Huai Raeng reservoir in Muang district of this eastern province as part of a crackdown on encroachment by investors.

data.title: Thailand showcases Thai massage and wellness at first national expo
data.description: Thailand is using Thai massage, traditional medicine and herbal innovation to expand its health economy through its first national wellness expo.

data.title: Your weekly horoscope for Aug 21-27
data.description: Your spot-on weekly horoscope for work, money and relationship from Guru by the Bangkok Post's famously accurate fortune teller. Let's see how you will fare this week and beyond.

data.title: 'So bad it's good': rough animated film becomes surprise Chinese hit
data.description: BEIJING - A low-budget Chinese animated film that was widely mocked for its crude visuals became a viral hit, with people packing cinemas to see just how bad it is.

data.title: Ex-Pakistan PM Khan taken back to jail after hospital checks
data.description: ISLAMABAD — Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan was transferred back to jail early on Friday, hours after being taken to a hospital for court-ordered medical checks, the government said.

data.title: 153,000 students and school staff affected in Canvas data breach
data.description: More than 153,000 students and staff from four tertiary institutions in Hong Kong have been affected by a data breach on the online learning management platform Canvas, an investigation by the city's privacy watchdog has found.

data.title: Nene Royal named Best New International Artiste in Ireland
data.description: Thai teenage rocker Nene Royal has been selected for the Best New International Artiste 2026 award in Dublin, extending her rise after America’s Got Talent.

data.title: Death toll from south China floods jumps to 159
data.description: BEIJING — The death toll from devastating floods in southern China last month jumped to 159 on Friday, state media reported, with ten people still missing.

data.title: Govt urged to create task force
data.description: <p>The Pollution Control Department (PCD) is asking the Natural Resources and Environment Ministry to establish a task force to tackle industrial waste problems after finding that illegal waste disposal cases are linked across several provinces.</p>

data.title: Over 20 Taiwanese cuffed over links to scam network
data.description: <p>Thailand and Taiwan have arrested more than 20 Taiwanese suspects allegedly linked to a call-centre scam network operating in Cambodia, with investigators now trying to identify the financiers behind the operation.</p>

data.title: People's Party aiming for Nonthaburi PAO presidency
data.description: <p>The opposition People's Party (PP) has launched its campaign for the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organisation (PAO) presidency, with candidate Decharut Sukkumnoed drawing ballot number 4 and urging residents to back him in the Sept 20 election.</p>

data.title: Thai government to review gun controls
data.description: <p>The government is preparing sweeping amendments to the country's gun control law, with the draft expected to reach the cabinet around mid-September after further public consultation, Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt says.</p>

data.title: Klatham merger 'will help Pheu Thai'
data.description: <p>Political commentator Jatuporn Prompan has warned that a possible merger between Pheu Thai and the Klatham Party could reshape the political landscape, potentially making Pheu Thai the second-largest party and challenging Bhumjaithai's position as the largest.</p>

data.title: SRT subsidiary readies for ARL takeover
data.description: <p>The State Railway of Thailand (SRT) is preparing its subsidiary to take over the Airport Rail Link when the current operator's contract ends next month.</p>
